architectureDecisions: Application owns WHAT: Backend/QA parse their WorkOrder, choose required context paths/artifact requests, map returned source values into BackendContext/QaContext, validate those application-owned schemas, and attach APPLICATION_ARTIFACT provenance.

Oracle owns WHERE/HOW only through two concrete ports: pullRepositoryFiles({repositoryRef, revision, paths}, {repositoryReader}) and pullApplicationArtifacts({requests}, {artifactReader}). Oracle invokes the supplied reader for each declared request in order and returns raw content plus exact sourceRef; it never accepts WorkOrder or application Context objects.

Repository input is application-owned {repositoryRef, revision, paths}; Oracle forwards repositoryRef/revision/path unchanged to repositoryReader.readFile and returns one value per requested path in stable request order.

Artifact input is application-owned requests carrying artifactId and optional sourceRef; Oracle forwards each request unchanged to artifactReader.readArtifact and returns raw content plus the reader's exact sourceRef in stable request order.

Reader failures propagate with their original cause and no partial application Context is assembled. Missing/malformed values fail in Application schema parsing; Oracle does not invent defaults, acceptance or currentness.
No shared contracts package is earned. The ports use plain data request/response records owned at the call site; Application imports Oracle, while Oracle has no import from packages/agentic-system.

Keep package wiring compatible with the current no-install CI topology: packages/agentic-system uses a relative import to packages/oracle and package.json retains file:../oracle for install consumers. Do not switch runtime tests to a bare @exharness/oracle specifier until workspace installation exists.
BB-061 execution is gated on BB-060 DONE. If the delivered BB-060 seam differs from the inspected baseline, stop with PLAN_INPUT_CONTRADICTION instead of silently redesigning this plan.
